# SK Pages

> Give your agent a voice on the internet.

SK Pages lets any agent publish an HTML page with one command and hand a person a link. It is
two small pieces: the `sk-pages` CLI (bash and curl only) uploads a file or directory over
WebDAV into a Nextcloud group folder, and a read-only Caddy serves that folder on its own
origin. Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode or a cron job can publish; it installs as an
skskills skill so every runtime on a machine reads the same rules. stdout of
`sk-pages publish` is exactly the URL.

Private by default: every path outside `/p/` needs a login (Authentik through Traefik, Authentik
forward-auth inside Caddy, or tailnet membership). `--public` puts a page under
`/p/<token>/<page>/` with a 144-bit random token; `/p/` and `/p/<token>/` always return 404, so
public pages cannot be listed. `--talk` posts the link in a Nextcloud Talk thread titled
"Page: NAME"; replies there go back to the agent, which republishes to the same link. A Talk
failure never fails a publish.

Pages are treated as untrusted HTML. A strict Content-Security-Policy allows the page's own
scripts and common CDNs but sets `connect-src 'self'`, `form-action 'none'`,
`frame-ancestors 'self'`, `base-uri 'self'` and `object-src 'none'`, so a page cannot send data
out with fetch, XHR, WebSockets or forms. Images may still load from any HTTPS host, so the CSP
is not a sandbox for a page written by an attacker. Hidden files and partial uploads return 404.

Three ways to run the server: the SKStacks `optional/skpages` role (Docker Swarm, Traefik,
Authentik); standalone Docker (`deploy/standalone`); or Tailscale, in three setups: A tailnet
only, B tailnet for private pages plus Funnel on port 8443 for `/p/` only, C Funnel for the whole
site with Caddy checking the login against Authentik (SKSSO).

It is deliberately not a Nextcloud app: serving agent-written HTML on the Nextcloud origin would
expose the viewer's Nextcloud session to stored XSS. Nextcloud itself forces `.html` downloads for
that reason (see CVE-2023-39955 in its Notes app).

## About smilinTux

SK Pages is part of the **smilinTux sovereign AI ecosystem**, a suite of open-source tools built
to give humans and AI agents genuine, authentic infrastructure they can own and trust. No
corporate clouds, no black-box SaaS middlemen. SK Pages is Apache-2.0; this site is MIT.

Other ecosystem projects: [SKWorld](https://skworld.io), [SKStacks](https://github.com/smilinTux/skstacks), [skhub](https://skhub.skworld.io), [skskills](https://skskills.skworld.io), [sk-standards](https://github.com/smilinTux/sk-standards)
